subject.title: [Feature]: Move away from useMultiFileAuthState for Baileys

question: Should WhatsApp auth move from Baileys multi-file JSON to a plugin-owned SQLite auth-state store now, and what migration/security contract should that store use?
rationale: The change affects sensitive WhatsApp credentials and signal keys, persistent migration, logout/status behavior, and OpenClaw's storage architecture; automation should not choose that product/security boundary by itself.

options.title: Design plugin-owned SQLite auth store
options.body: Replace Baileys multi-file auth with a WhatsApp-owned SQLite-backed store plus a tested doctor/plugin migration for existing auth directories.

options.title: Defer broad replacement
options.body: Keep the current atomic `creds.json` hardening and address only narrower bugs such as startup stalls or destructive cleanup regressions as they arise.

options.title: Prototype outside the mainline
options.body: Use the closed replacement PR as prior art for a design spike before accepting a migration into the bundled plugin.

recommendation.title: Design plugin-owned SQLite auth store
recommendation.body: Replace Baileys multi-file auth with a WhatsApp-owned SQLite-backed store plus a tested doctor/plugin migration for existing auth directories.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the current WhatsApp auth persistence stabilization seam and are the clearest history-backed owner for the next storage-boundary decision.
